text: Given `Shape c = new Circle(1);`, calling `c.area()` runs `Circle.area`, but the overloaded call `describe(c)` selects the `Shape` version. Why do the two disagree?
choices: Overriding is resolved at run time from the object's actual type; overload resolution happens at compile time from the reference's declared type.
The cast to `Circle` was omitted, so the JVM discards the subclass method table.
`describe` is static, and static methods ignore inheritance entirely.
Overloaded methods are always resolved against the superclass, regardless of the declared type.
explanation: Two different resolution rules meet in one line. `c.area()` compiles to invokevirtual, which follows the object's class pointer to `Circle.area`. `describe(c)` was resolved by the compiler, which knew only that `c` was declared `Shape`. Writing `describe((Circle) c)` selects the other overload, because the cast changes the declared type at that call site.
